acceptance: The Harness package exposes a small provider-neutral EventStore contract that consumes existing validated EventRecord values and has no dependency on a concrete database, model/provider, browser, or UI framework.
Focused tests prove the zero-based contiguous sequence invariant for each Run, independent Run isolation, immutable append-only history, and deterministic ascending replay.

Duplicate event identity, duplicate sequence position, skipped sequence, regressed sequence, cross-Run substitution, and invalid EventRecord input fail closed with stable machine-readable error/result semantics and cannot mutate accepted history.
Repeated reads/replay of the same accepted history are deterministic, do not mutate stored records, and preserve exact EventRecord identity/content.
The implementation and evidence explicitly state that the in-memory reference is not durable persistence; a later bounded adapter Grain is required before parent IN-P03-S01-T01 can close.

Any implementation candidate must pass repository format/lint/typecheck/tests, truthful Diffcipline proof, checksum-verified Alibaba Open Code Review, required credentialed Jev semantic review, exact-head CI, normal merge, and fresh-main CI before closure.

required: Exact base/head/merge-base and complete changed-file accounting.
Focused append/replay invariant tests plus full repository format/lint/typecheck/test suites.
Diffcipline proof, Alibaba OCR evidence, credentialed Jev semantic review, exact-head semantic review, and post-merge fresh-main CI.

minimality.rationale: Reuse SG-000011 EventRecord validation and SG-000038 Run semantics. Define only the provider-neutral append/replay boundary and deterministic reference behavior now; defer durable storage and operational adapters to an independently reviewable Grain.

requirements: Event presence, sequence position, or successful append never grants capability, authorization, credential, network, provider, release, deployment, or PASS authority.
Accepted event history is immutable and fail-closed under identity/sequence conflict; no silent overwrite, gap repair, or cross-Run substitution is allowed.
The reference implementation is deterministic and side-effect bounded; durable persistence is explicitly deferred rather than simulated or fabricated.

outcome: The Harness Kernel has a deterministic provider-neutral EventStore contract and reference semantics for validated EventRecord append/replay, with zero-based contiguous per-Run ordering, immutable history, conflict rejection, and no capability authority before any durable database adapter is introduced.
rationale: SG-000011 defined EventRecord wire validation, SG-000038 shaped Run lifecycle/continuation semantics, and the current session shell already emits per-Run zero-based sequences in memory. P03-S01 still lacks a canonical event-store boundary. The smallest safe next step is to define append/replay semantics independently from Supabase, network, providers, artifacts, and budgets so durable persistence can be implemented and reviewed as a later adapter Grain.

risk.recovery: Revert only the new Harness EventStore contract/reference implementation and exports; SG-000011 protocol records, SG-000038 Run lifecycle shaping, and existing session-shell behavior remain intact.

scope_in: Introduce the minimal P03 Harness Kernel package boundary needed to own provider-neutral Run event-store semantics without moving or redefining SG-000011 protocol records.
Define an EventStore port over validated EventRecord values with append and per-Run ordered read/replay behavior; the store must not invent, repair, or silently coerce invalid protocol records.

Define canonical per-Run ordering as zero-based contiguous sequence values: the first persisted event for a Run is sequence 0 and each subsequent event is exactly the prior persisted sequence plus one.

Make event history append-only and immutable: reject duplicate event identities, duplicate per-Run sequence positions, sequence gaps, sequence regression, and any attempt to overwrite or mutate an already accepted event.
Require deterministic Run isolation and replay: reading a Run returns only that Run's accepted events in ascending sequence order, independent of insertion/query implementation details or other Runs.

Allow a deterministic in-memory reference implementation for contract qualification while explicitly preserving that it is not durable persistence and does not close the parent P03-S01 task by itself.
scope_out: No Supabase/Postgres/database schema, migration, durable storage adapter, network call, secret, browser storage, filesystem persistence, queue, cache, or hosted service operation.
No change to EventRecord or RunRecord wire schemas, no new timestamps/cost/provider fields, no lifecycle state mutation, and no automatic derivation of Run state from event presence.
No artifact store, budget governor, model/provider/tool routing, retry execution, scheduler, capability grant, evidence PASS authority, release/deployment behavior, or P02 changes.
title: IN-P03-S01-T01B provider-neutral append-only Run event-store contract
